label: Game of Thrones
rubric: Power & influence · Character arc · Fan popularity · Memorable moments

entries.name: Tyrion Lannister
entries.rationale: The show's sharpest wit and moral center, carried almost single-handedly by Peter Dinklage's performance.

entries.name: Jon Snow
entries.rationale: The reluctant hero whose arc from bastard to king (and back) anchored the entire saga.

entries.name: Arya Stark
entries.rationale: A fan-favorite revenge arc that ended with her killing the Night King himself.

entries.name: Daenerys Targaryen
entries.rationale: Mother of Dragons whose rise and fall became the show's most debated storyline.

entries.name: Cersei Lannister
entries.rationale: One of television's great villains, ruthless and utterly convinced of her own righteousness.

entries.name: Eddard 'Ned' Stark
entries.rationale: His shocking season-one death redefined what audiences could expect from the genre.

entries.name: Jaime Lannister
entries.rationale: The Kingslayer's slow redemption arc is one of the show's most complete character journeys.

entries.name: Sandor 'The Hound' Clegane
entries.rationale: Brutal, funny, and unexpectedly tender — a fan favorite from start to finish.

entries.name: Tywin Lannister
entries.rationale: Cold, commanding, and the true power behind the Iron Throne for years.

entries.name: Petyr 'Littlefinger' Baelish
entries.rationale: The master manipulator whose schemes quietly shaped nearly every major plot turn.

entries.name: Oberyn Martell
entries.rationale: A single season was enough to make the Red Viper one of the most beloved characters ever.

entries.name: Brienne of Tarth
entries.rationale: A knight in every sense but title, and one of the show's most honorable figures.

entries.name: Varys
entries.rationale: The spider whose loyalty to 'the realm' made him impossible to fully trust or dismiss.

entries.name: Olenna Tyrell
entries.rationale: The Queen of Thorns delivered some of the show's best lines right up to her final scene.

entries.name: Ramsay Bolton
entries.rationale: A villain so cruel he became the character fans most wanted to see fall.

entries.name: Robb Stark
entries.rationale: The King in the North whose Red Wedding fate remains one of TV's most shocking moments.

entries.name: Joffrey Baratheon
entries.rationale: Petulant and sadistic, he became the most hated character on television for good reason.

entries.name: Theon Greyjoy
entries.rationale: A betrayal-to-redemption arc that put him through more suffering than almost anyone else.

entries.name: Khal Drogo
entries.rationale: Imposing and iconic despite a relatively short run in the story.

entries.name: Davos Seaworth
entries.rationale: The Onion Knight's quiet decency made him one of the show's most trusted moral compasses.

entries.name: Bronn
entries.rationale: The sellsword whose blunt pragmatism provided some of the sharpest comic relief in Westeros.

entries.name: Bran Stark
entries.rationale: From crippled boy to Three-Eyed Raven to, controversially, King of the Six Kingdoms.

entries.name: Catelyn Stark
entries.rationale: A fiercely protective mother whose choices set several of the war's tragedies in motion.

entries.name: Stannis Baratheon
entries.rationale: Rigid, humorless, and strangely compelling in his unwavering sense of duty.

entries.name: Samwell Tarly
entries.rationale: The unlikely scholar who ended up shaping the future of the realm from the Citadel.

entries.name: Melisandre
entries.rationale: The Red Woman's prophecies and fire magic kept the story's supernatural stakes alive.

entries.name: Robert Baratheon
entries.rationale: A once-great warrior gone soft on the throne, setting the whole series in motion.

entries.name: Margaery Tyrell
entries.rationale: A political operator as sharp as any Lannister, undone by an explosive finale.

entries.name: Grey Worm
entries.rationale: The Unsullied commander whose loyalty to Daenerys never wavered.

entries.name: Missandei
entries.rationale: Advisor and translator whose death became one of the final season's most gutting moments.
